title: Interference and diffraction of light
summary: Learn about Young's experiment, fringe spacing, single-slit diffraction, and polarization.
cards.0.p: According to Huygens, every point of a wavefront is a source that sends out small wavelets. The common tangent of these wavelets forms the new wavefront. This principle explains diffraction and refraction.
cards.0.key: Diffraction is the spreading of a wave that passes through a narrow gap. The principle holds for water waves as well as for light.
cards.1.h: Young's experiment: light is a wave
cards.1.p: In 1801 Young passed light of a single color through two narrow slits. On the screen he saw bright and dark fringes. Darkness forming where light falls on light can only be explained by the interference of waves.
cards.1.key: Newton thought light was a stream of particles, and Huygens thought it was a wave. The double-slit pattern shows most clearly that light behaves like a wave.
cards.1.once.soru: If you pass single-color light through two narrow slits onto a screen, what do you see?
cards.1.once.secenekler.0.neden: The waves from the two slits interfere. So bright and dark fringes form in turn.
cards.1.once.secenekler.1.neden: That would happen if light were only particles. But the experiment shows an interference pattern.
cards.1.once.secenekler.2.neden: The waves cancel each other at some points. That is why dark bands form.
cards.2.p: The two slits behave like two sources in phase. The path difference of the rays reaching point P is Δ = |r2 − r1|. If the screen is far away, Δ ≈ d·sinθ.
cards.2.key: θ is the angle between the direction of the center and the direction of P. Whether P is bright or dark is decided by the ratio of Δ to λ.
cards.2.once.soru: Point P is 5.0 µm from S₁ and 6.2 µm from S₂. What is the path difference?
cards.2.once.secenekler.0.neden: The path difference is the difference of the two distances: 6.2 − 5.0.
cards.2.once.secenekler.1.neden: The distances are subtracted, not added.
cards.2.once.secenekler.2.neden: That is only the distance to S₂. You have to take the difference of the two distances.
cards.3.h: Conditions for bright and dark fringes
cards.3.p: If the path difference is a whole multiple of λ (Δ = n·λ), there is constructive interference and a bright fringe forms. If it is a half multiple (Δ = (n − ½)·λ), there is destructive interference and a dark fringe forms.
cards.3.key: For example, if Δ = 2λ, this is the 2nd bright fringe. If Δ = 2.5λ, this is the 3rd dark fringe.
cards.4.h: Distance of the fringes from the center
cards.4.p: At the center the path difference is zero, and the central bright fringe forms there. At a distance x from the center, Δ ≈ d·x/L. The nth bright fringe is at a distance x = n·λL/d from the center.
cards.4.key: The nth dark fringe is at a distance x = (n − ½)·λL/d from the center. The pattern is symmetric about the center.
cards.5.p: The distance between two neighboring bright fringes is called the fringe spacing: Δx = λ·L/d. If λ or L increases the fringes spread apart, and if d increases they get closer. The intensity of the light does not change Δx.
cards.5.key: In red light the fringes are wider than in violet, because red has a longer wavelength.
cards.5.etk.soru: Change the wavelength, the screen distance, and the slit separation: Δx = λL/d.
cards.6.p: Let λ = 450 nm, d = 0.25 mm, and L = 1 m. Then Δx = 1.8 mm. The 2nd bright fringe is 3.6 mm away, and the 1st dark fringe is 0.9 mm away.
cards.6.key: Δx = (4.5×10⁻⁷ · 1) / (2.5×10⁻⁴) m. A common mistake is to calculate without converting nm to 10⁻⁹ m and mm to 10⁻³ m.
cards.6.once.soru: λ = 450 nm, d = 0.25 mm, L = 1 m. What is the fringe spacing Δx = λL/d in mm?
cards.6.once.secenekler.1.neden: When you convert the units to meters, the result comes out 10 times smaller.
cards.6.once.secenekler.2.neden: 1 nm is 10⁻⁹ m, and 1 mm is 10⁻³ m. The result is 1.8×10⁻³ m.
cards.7.h: If the setup is put under water
cards.7.p: When the setup is immersed in a liquid of refractive index n, the frequency does not change. The wavelength becomes n times smaller: λ′ = λ/n. The fringe spacing gets smaller too: Δx′ = Δx/n.
cards.7.svg#7: frequency unchanged; speed and λ decrease
cards.7.key: The path difference at the center is still zero. So the central bright fringe stays in the middle.
cards.8.h: Where does the central fringe shift?
cards.8.p: If a thin transparent plate is placed in front of one of the slits, the light on that path is delayed. In this case the central fringe shifts toward the plate. If the source is moved, the central fringe shifts the opposite way.
cards.8.svg#6: the center shifts toward the slit with the plate
cards.8.key: In both cases the fringe spacing does not change. The whole pattern shifts together.
cards.8.once.soru: A thin piece of glass is placed in front of the upper slit. Where does the central bright fringe shift?
cards.8.once.secenekler.0.neden: The glass delays the light on the upper path. So the point where the two beams meet with equal delay shifts toward the glass.
cards.8.once.secenekler.1.neden: Since the delay is on the upper path, the balance point shifts to the upper side.
cards.8.once.secenekler.2.neden: Since the glass delays the light on one path, the point of zero path difference changes.
cards.9.p: In white light, each color forms its own pattern. At the center the path difference is zero for all colors. That is why the central fringe is white. The inner edge of the side fringes is violet, and the outer edge is red.
cards.9.svg#6: 1st fringe: violet inside, red outside; farther out colors mix
cards.9.key: Violet light has the shortest wavelength, so its fringes are closest to the center. Farther from the center, the colors mix.
cards.9.once.soru: If Young's experiment is done with white light, what color is the central fringe?
cards.9.once.secenekler.0.neden: At the center all colors interfere constructively and combine into white.
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.neden: Violet fringes are closest to the center, but all colors meet at the center.
cards.9.once.secenekler.2.neden: Red fringes are farthest from the center.
cards.10.p: Light passing through a single narrow slit also forms a pattern. For a slit of width w, the condition for a dark fringe is w·sinθ = n·λ. The central fringe is twice as wide as the side fringes.
cards.10.key: The width of a side fringe is λL/w. For a dark fringe in a single slit you write n·λ. Do not confuse this with (n − ½)·λ for the double slit.
cards.11.p: In a double slit the fringes are equally wide and similar in brightness. In a single slit the central fringe is wide and bright, and the sides are faint. As the slit gets narrower, the pattern widens.
cards.11.key: Diffraction is pronounced when the slit is comparable to the wavelength. Sound bends around a doorway, but light hardly does. That is because the wavelength of sound is about 1 m, and that of light is about 500 nm.
cards.11.once.soru: On the screen there is a pattern with a very wide, bright middle and faint sides. What did the light pass through?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: In a single slit the central fringe is twice as wide, and the sides fade quickly.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: In a double slit the fringes are about equal in width and brightness.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: A prism splits light into its colors, but it does not form a bright-dark pattern.
cards.12.p: In a soap bubble or a thin layer of oil on water, part of the light reflects from the top surface of the film and part from the bottom surface. These two rays interfere, and the film looks colored.
cards.12.svg#8: color depends on film thickness and viewing angle
cards.12.svg#9: soap bubble, oil layer on water
cards.12.key: The thickness of the film and the viewing angle decide which color gets stronger. A very thin soap film looks dark, because one of the reflected rays is shifted by half a wave.
cards.12.once.soru: Why does a soap bubble look colored?
cards.12.once.secenekler.0.neden: The rays reflected from the two surfaces of the film strengthen some colors and cancel others.
cards.12.once.secenekler.1.neden: Colorless soap also makes colored bubbles.
cards.12.once.secenekler.2.neden: The colors come from interference, not from absorption.
cards.13.h: Polarization: light is a transverse wave
cards.13.p: What vibrates in light is the electric field. A polarizer lets through only the vibration in a single direction. Only transverse waves can be polarized. Light is a transverse wave, and sound cannot be polarized.
cards.13.svg#6: only transverse waves can be polarized
cards.13.key: Two polarizers turned 90° to each other block light completely. Polarized sunglasses cut the glare reflected from water and roads.
cards.14.p:
• Young's experiment shows that light is a wave.
• For bright fringes Δ = n·λ, and for dark fringes Δ = (n − ½)·λ.
• The fringe spacing is Δx = λL/d and drops to Δx/n in a liquid.
• In a single slit the central fringe is 2 times as wide.
• Polarization proves that light is a transverse wave.
cards.14.svg#1: bright Δ = nλ · dark Δ = (n − ½)λ
cards.14.svg#2: Δx = λL/d · in a liquid Δx/n
quiz.0.q: In Young's experiment, λ = 500 nm, the slit separation is d = 0.25 mm, and the screen distance is L = 2 m. How many mm is it from the central bright fringe to the 3rd bright fringe?
quiz.0.e: Δx = λL/d = (5×10<sup>−7</sup> · 2)/(2.5×10<sup>−4</sup>) = 4×10<sup>−3</sup> m = 4 mm. The 3rd bright fringe is 3·Δx = 12 mm from the center.
quiz.1.q: In the double-slit experiment, match the path difference (Δ) at point P with the fringe observed.
quiz.1.e: For a bright fringe Δ = n·λ, and for a dark fringe Δ = (n − ½)·λ. So 0.5λ is the n = 1 dark fringe, and 1.5λ is the n = 2 dark fringe.
quiz.2.q: How does each change affect the fringe spacing (Δx = λL/d) in Young's experiment? (λ: wavelength, L: screen distance, d: slit separation)
quiz.2.e: Δx is directly proportional to λ and L, and inversely proportional to d. In water the wavelength is λ/n, so Δx is divided by n too. The intensity of the light only makes the fringes brighter and does not change the spacing.
quiz.3.q: In a single-slit diffraction experiment, if the slit is made narrower, what can be said about the central bright fringe?
quiz.3.e: The width of the central fringe is 2λL/w. When w gets smaller, this width increases. Diffraction becomes more pronounced as the slit approaches the wavelength.
quiz.3.y.0: The width of the central fringe is 2λL/w. As the slit narrows, the light spreads more and the fringe widens.
quiz.3.y.1: The fringe width depends on the width of the slit. When w gets smaller, 2λL/w grows and the fringe widens.
quiz.3.y.3: All the wavelets reach the center in phase. So a bright fringe always forms there, and the fringe only widens.
A:ozet: Pass a wave through a narrow gap and find a fringe in Young's experiment. Work out the path difference, change the fringe spacing, and put the setup under water. Narrow a single slit and block light with a polarizer.
A:adimlar.0.metin: A plane wave passes through a gap in a barrier. Narrow the gap and see the wave spread in every direction.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: When the gap narrows to about one wavelength, a single wavelet source is left there and the wave spreads like a semicircle. This is called diffraction. In a wide gap the common tangent of the wavelets is still a plane front, and the wave bends only a little at the edges.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.ipucu: Diffraction is pronounced when the gap is comparable to the wavelength.
A:adimlar.1.metin: At a bright fringe the path difference is a whole multiple of λ. The path difference of the rays reaching P from S₁ and S₂ is Δ = d·x/L. Slide P and find the 2nd bright fringe.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.tamam: At x = 6 mm, Δ = 1200 nm = 2λ. The waves meet crest to crest and interfere constructively. In this setup the fringe spacing is 3 mm. So the 2nd bright fringe is 2 · 3 = 6 mm from the center.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.ipucu: The path difference must be exactly 2 wavelengths: Δ = 1200 nm.
A:adimlar.2.metin: If the path difference is a whole multiple of λ a bright fringe forms, and if it is a half multiple a dark fringe forms. Here λ = 500 nm. The light reaching P from S₂ travels 1750 nm farther than the light from S₁.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: What is seen at point P?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: For a bright fringe, Δ must be a whole multiple of the wavelength. 1750 / 500 = 3.5 is not a whole number.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: At the 3rd dark fringe, Δ would be (3 − ½)·λ = 2.5λ = 1250 nm.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Δ/λ = 3.5 = 4 − ½. A crest meets a trough and there is destructive interference. Since the dark fringe condition is Δ = (n − ½)·λ, n = 4.
A:adimlar.3.metin: The fringe spacing is found with Δx = λ·L/d. Change the wavelength, the screen distance, and the slit separation. Turn on the light each time and look at the pattern.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.soru: What should you do to bring the fringes closer together?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: As the slits moved apart, the fringes got closer. You will see the reason in the relation Δx = λL/d on the next card.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Red has a longer wavelength. When λ grows, Δx grows too and the fringes spread apart.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The intensity of the light does not change Δx. The fringes only get brighter.
A:adimlar.4.baslik: If the setup is put under water
A:adimlar.4.metin: In air the fringe spacing is 4 mm. Now we will immerse the whole setup in water, which has a refractive index of 1.33.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.soru: What happens to the fringes on the screen?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: In water the wavelength of light becomes 1.33 times smaller. The fringe spacing shrinks by the same ratio: 4 / 1.33 ≈ 3 mm.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: For the fringes to spread apart, the wavelength would have to grow. But in water the wavelength shrinks.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Even though the frequency stays the same, Δx = λL/d depends on the wavelength. In water λ shrinks.
A:adimlar.5.metin: The width of the central bright fringe is 2λL/w (λ = 500 nm, L = 1 m). Adjust the slit so that the central fringe is 20 mm wide.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.tamam: For w = 50 μm, 2 · 500 nm · 1 m / 50 μm = 20 mm. As the slit narrows, the pattern widens.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.ipucu: The width of the central fringe is inversely proportional to w. To widen the fringe, narrow the slit.
A:adimlar.6.metin: A polarizer lets light through only with its vibrations in a single direction. Turn the second polarizer so that no light reaches the screen.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.tamam: When the second polarizer is turned 90° relative to the first, the light is blocked completely. At in-between angles, part of the light gets through.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.ipucu: The transmitted light goes out when the directions of the two polarizers are perpendicular.
A:kapanis.0: According to Huygens' principle, every point of a wavefront is a new source. In a narrow gap the wave is diffracted.
A:kapanis.1: Young's experiment shows that light is a wave.
A:kapanis.2: For a bright fringe Δ = n·λ, and for a dark fringe Δ = (n − ½)·λ.
A:kapanis.3: The fringe spacing is found with Δx = λL/d. If the setup is immersed in a liquid, the fringe spacing becomes Δx/n.
A:kapanis.4: In a single slit the width of the central fringe is 2λL/w. When the slit narrows, the pattern widens.
A:kapanis.5: Polarization proves that light is a transverse wave.
